facts.text: Walnut Creek was named after the Arroyo de las Nueces, the Spanish for walnut creek, which in turn was named for the native walnut tree Juglans hindsii.
The arrival of Southern Pacific Railroad service in 1891 sparked rapid growth and turned Walnut Creek into a thriving rail town.
Shadelands Ranch, once owned by the Penniman family, now houses the Walnut Creek Historical Society museum where visitors can explore local heritage.
Walnut Creek’s own government‑access television channel, WCTV, broadcasts local government and community events and is available on Comcast channel 28.
Metallica drummer Lars Ulrich, a globally recognized musician, was born in Walnut Creek, adding a rock‑star connection to the city.
